phenomena.label: Coordinate Structure Constraint / embedded negative declarative na(d)
phenomena.hypothesis: Models must track island constraints on coordinate structures alongside the embedded negative declarative particle na(d), a long-distance dependency that is hard to learn from surface statistics.
phenomena.note: Aoife, Tier 1. CSC with embedded negative declarative na(d).

phenomena.label: Anti-agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: Anti-agreement suppresses expected verb agreement under extraction, an anti-pattern that contradicts the general agreement statistics a model learns.

phenomena.label: Binding (anaphora / Principle A)
phenomena.hypothesis: Anaphors require a structurally local antecedent, a c-command relation that surface proximity heuristics fail to capture.

phenomena.label: Possessor extraction
phenomena.hypothesis: Extracting a possessor out of a DP is a rare long-distance dependency that stresses a model's island sensitivity.

phenomena.label: Superiority
phenomena.hypothesis: Superiority governs which of multiple wh-elements may move first, a hierarchical constraint invisible to linear-order models.

phenomena.label: Adjective number agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: Welsh adjectives can inflect for number and must agree with the noun, a low-frequency agreement pattern models tend to ignore.
phenomena.note: Lily, Tier 1. Part of agreement bundle: adjective number, definiteness, pronoun agreement, conjuncts.

phenomena.label: Definiteness agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: Definiteness must be consistently marked across the nominal, and models may mismatch article and noun definiteness.

phenomena.label: Pronoun agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: Welsh pronouns must agree in person/number/gender with their controllers, straining models on rich morphological paradigms.

phenomena.label: Conjunct agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: Agreement with coordinated conjuncts can be resolved or closest-conjunct based, an ambiguity that confuses purely distributional models.

phenomena.label: Negation dependent constraint (ddim)
phenomena.hypothesis: The negator ddim is licensed only in specific dependent contexts, a distributional restriction easily overgeneralised.

phenomena.label: Bod-clauses
phenomena.hypothesis: Non-finite bod complement clauses require special selection and mutation, a construction that is structurally distinct from finite clauses.

phenomena.label: Clitics in passive contexts
phenomena.hypothesis: Clitic placement interacts with passive voice in ways that decouple form from thematic role, challenging surface models.

phenomena.label: Resumption strategies
phenomena.hypothesis: Resumptive pronouns fill gaps in certain relative-clause and extraction contexts, and their obligatory-vs-illicit distribution requires careful minimal pairs.
phenomena.note: Suchir, Tier 1. Set up minimal pairs carefully.

phenomena.label: Pied-piping
phenomena.hypothesis: Pied-piping moves a larger phrase with the wh-element, and whether it is allowed depends on context in ways models under-learn.

phenomena.label: Particles (yn; aspectual particle)
phenomena.hypothesis: The particle yn has predicative and aspectual functions with distinct triggers and mutation effects that models conflate.
phenomena.note: Suchir, Tier 1. yn; the aspectual particle.

phenomena.label: Adverb position (verbal syntax)
phenomena.hypothesis: Adverb placement is constrained by the verbal syntax of VSO Welsh, and illicit positions are hard to detect from linear order alone.

phenomena.label: Imperative
phenomena.hypothesis: Imperative verb forms and subject licensing differ from declaratives, a low-frequency mood contrast for models.

phenomena.label: Null subjects
phenomena.hypothesis: Pro-drop is licensed by rich agreement, and models must connect a null argument to inflectional cues rather than an overt token.

phenomena.label: Quantifiers (dim)
phenomena.hypothesis: The quantifier dim has restricted distribution interacting with negation, easily overgeneralised by models.

phenomena.label: dim / mo
phenomena.hypothesis: The alternation between dim and the contracted mo before definite objects is a fine-grained morphosyntactic contrast.

phenomena.label: placeholder
phenomena.hypothesis: dup

phenomena.label: Agreement – focus
phenomena.hypothesis: Focus fronting alters agreement marking, decoupling agreement from canonical subject position in ways models struggle to track.
phenomena.note: Tier 2. To do: add dialectal syntax / notes of speaker variation.
